text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Payments on Bulgaria's foreign debt will be a priority for the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) despite limited BNB foreign exchange reserves and lower than expected proceeds from privatisation in 1996, BNB governor Lyubomir Filipov said. @

-- Bulgaria's President Zhelyu Zhelev said he would start consultations with parliamentary groups today on the formation of a new government following the resignation of Prime Minister Zhan Videnov and his cabinet.
-- Bulgaria's outgoing cabinet decided to offer two pipeline concessions for transiting Russian gas through the country, a senior government official said.
-- Bulgaria's outgoing cabinet postponed debate on the 1997 draft budget to January 3. @

-- Belgium's chemicals company Solvay SA has transfered $30 million from a total of $160 million for the 60 percent stake in Bulgaria's soda ash producer Sodi-Devnya it bought this month, Privatisation Agency executive director Vesselin Blagoev said.
Blagoev also said Bulgaria was expected to open a privatisation tender for the chemicals producer Himko-Vratsa after January 25.

-- Bulgaria's main opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) leader Ivan Kostov presented evidence on an alleged illegal phone tapping at the UDF headquarters to the outgiong Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev.
-- Bulgaria completed 509 privatisation deals worth some 96 billion levs in 1996, the Privatisation Agency said.
-- The bodies of another nine people frozen to death in snow storms in Bulgaria since December 24 have been found, bringing the death toll to 19. @
-- Monthly inflation for December is expected at 15 percent and cumulative annual inflation for 1996 is seen at 270 percent, financial experts said.

-- Bulgaria's main opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) said it planned to stage a rally in Sofia on January 3 against the policy of the ruling Socialist party, UDF officials said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
